questions.q: Where does Yahweh tell Jeremiah to go to hear a word from him?
questions.a: Yahweh tells Jeremiah to go to the potter’s house.

questions.q: What did Jeremiah see the potter doing at his house?
questions.a: Jeremiah saw the potter working at his wheel, shaping clay.

questions.q: What happened to the object of clay that the potter molded while Jeremiah was watching?
questions.a: It was ruined in his hand, so he started over.

questions.q: To what does Yahweh compare the house of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh compares Israel to clay in the potter’s hand.

questions.q: What might Yahweh say he will do to a nation or kingdom?
questions.a: He might say he will uproot, tear down, and destroy it.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to a nation that turns from evil after it hears his proclamation?
questions.a: He will relent from the disaster that he was planning to bring upon it.

questions.q: What might Yahweh say he will do for a nation or kingdom?
questions.a: He might say he will build it up and help it grow.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to a nation that does not listen to his voice?
questions.a: He will not do the good that he had said he would do for them.

questions.q: Why will Yahweh form disaster against the people of Judah and Jerusalem?
questions.a: They are doing wicked things.

questions.q: What will the men of Judah and Jerusalem do after Jeremiah warns them?
questions.a: They will not listen or stop doing evil things.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say Israel has done?
questions.a: Yahweh says Israel has done a very horrible thing that no other nation has done.

questions.q: According to Yahweh, what happens to the snow of Lebanon and its cold mountain streams?
questions.a: They never melt away or dry up.

questions.q: What have the people of Israel done that shows they have forgotten Yahweh?
questions.a: They have forgotten Yahweh and burned incense to worthless idols.

questions.q: Why will everyone who passes by shudder and shake his head?
questions.a: They will do that because Yahweh has made the land an empty wasteland.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do to his people when disaster comes?
questions.a: He will scatter them before their enemies and refuse to help them.

questions.q: What is the people’s plot against Jeremiah?
questions.a: They plan to attack him with their words and no longer pay attention to anything he says.

questions.q: What does Jeremiah ask Yahweh to do at the start of his prayer?
questions.a: He asks Yahweh to pay attention to him and listen to what his enemies are saying.

questions.q: What does Jeremiah ask Yahweh to remember him for?
questions.a: Jeremiah asks Yahweh to remember how he had spoken for the people’s welfare.

questions.q: What does Jeremiah ask Yahweh to do to his enemies?
questions.a: He asks Yahweh to let their children starve, their wives become widows, and their men be killed by the sword in battle.

questions.q: What does Jeremiah ask Yahweh to suddenly send against his enemies?
questions.a: He asks Yahweh to send a raiding army against them.

questions.q: What does Jeremiah ask Yahweh not to do for his enemies?
questions.a: He asks Yahweh not to forgive their sin or wrongdoing.

commentary.text: God's power over his creatures is represented by the potter. (Jer. 18:1-10) The Jews exhorted to repentance, and judgments foretold. (Jer. 18:11-17) The prophet appeals to God. (Jer. 18:18-23)

Jer. 18:1-10 While Jeremiah looks upon the potter's work, God darts into his mind two great truths. God has authority, and power, to form and fashion kingdoms and nations as he pleases. He may dispose of us as he thinks fit; and it would be as absurd for us to dispute this, as for the clay to quarrel with the potter. But he always goes by fixed rules of justice and goodness. When God is coming against us in judgments, we may be sure it is for our sins; but sincere conversion from the evil of sin will prevent the evil of punishment, as to persons, and to families, and nations.

Jer. 18:11-17 Sinners call it liberty to live at large; whereas for a man to be a slave to his lusts, is the very worst slavery. They forsook God for idols. When men are parched with heat, and meet with cooling, refreshing streams, they use them. In these things men will not leave a certainty for an uncertainty; but Israel left the ancient paths appointed by the Divine law. They walked not in the highway, in which they might travel safely, but in a way in which they must stumble: such was the way of idolatry, and such is the way of iniquity. This made their land desolate, and themselves miserable. Calamities may be borne, if God smile upon us when under them; but if he is displeased, and refuses his help, we are undone. Multitudes forget the Lord and his Christ, and wander from the ancient paths, to walk in ways of their own devising. But what will they do in the day of judgment!

Jer. 18:18-23 When the prophet called to repentance, instead of obeying the call, the people devised devices against him. Thus do sinners deal with the great Intercessor, crucifying him afresh, and speaking against him on earth, while his blood is speaking for them in heaven. But the prophet had done his duty to them; and the same will be our rejoicing in a day of evil.
